Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency looks promising. Before we spin up our POC we need to confirm a couple of privacy points for our legal team related to children under 13 (COPPA territory). Two short asks: 

1) Do you have a formal attestation that Redwood does not knowingly collect or retain personal information from users under 13 without parental consent?
2) Can you point me to the precise DPA language we can include for the POC that references COPPA/age-gating requirements and parental consent responsibilities?

Our architects will also want a simplified data flow diagram showing where tokens and logs are stored and for how long (we can sign an NDA if needed).

Would appreciate a reply by EOD Friday if possible — contract kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: COPPA Attestation and DPA language (EduPlay POC)

Liam — attaching the artifacts requested. Summary below.

Summary:
- COPPA Attestation: Redwood does not knowingly collect or retain personal information from children under 13 through customer integrations. Customers are required to implement age-gating and obtain parental consent when deploying services intended for children under 13. Attached: COPPA_Attestation_Letter.pdf (formal attestation).
- DPA language: We provided a redlineable clause to be appended to the DPA that makes responsibilities explicit ("Customer responsibilities: age verification, parental consent acquisition, and parental requests"). Attached: DPA_COPPA_clause.pdf
- SOC 2 reference: For operational controls relevant to data retention, logging, access control, see SOC2_summary.pdf (summary of relevant control families).
- DPIA / data flow: David attached a simplified DataFlow_DPIA.xlsx that maps ephemeral token handling, KV-cache retention (default 0-24h depending on config), and audit log retention options. If you require a full DPIA we can run a scoped exercise; let us know the jurisdiction and processing basis.

A couple of practical notes:
- Age-gating implementation may be stricter in the EU under local laws; Redwood’s platform supports configurable session TTLs and redaction hooks but does not host end-user age verification flows — that remains the responsibility of the customer integration.
- If EduPlay wants us to perform POP (proof of parental consent) verification (e.g., accept signed consent forms via our control plane), we can discuss an integration, but it will be scoped as an add-on (and may require Dedicated/Private deployment for evidence retention guarantees).

Attachments included: COPPA_Attestation_Letter.pdf, DPA_COPPA_clause.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf, DataFlow_DPIA.xlsx

If you can confirm who (EduPlay or developers) will handle age checks, we can finalize the DPA wording and produce a short DPIA addendum for your legal team.

Rgds,
Rachel Kim
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Age verification: EduPlay will own the age-gate and parental consent flow for the POC (we already have a minimal flow in place).
